2 Phd and 2 post-docs openings at HCI Sorbonne (Paris, France)

PhD 1 — Computational Interaction: Efficient interaction through maximization of mutual information. How can general principles from information theory, specifically measures of how much information is exchanged between user and system, be used to guide interface design in a more universal way? More information at

PhD 2 — From the Lab to the Wild: Improving External Validity in HCI. In collaboration with LOKI (Lille). Controlled experiments in HCI provide clean and controlled comparisons, but they often fail to capture the complexity of real-world use. This PhD addresses this gap by studying how interaction techniques perform “in the wild” and developing better ways to evaluate them in realistic settings. More information at

Post-doc 1 — Navigation (eg Google Maps) as an information-theoretic inference process. Redesign google maps: Develop general computational principles for guiding interaction based on information gain, rather than focusing on specific interface design choices

Post-doc 2 — In collaboration with Mehdi Khamassi and Gilles Bailly. Computational models of collaboration with and without artificial agents, and how they could be exploited to design interventions in interactive systems.

HCI Sorbonne:

Application reviewed on a rolling basis. To apply to a PhD, follow the instructions on the associated links. Application materials for post-docs:
- Cover letter
- CV
- 1–3 representative manuscripts
- Names and contact information for at least two references
- send to julien.gori@cnrs.fr

Questions may be directed to Julien Gori, Researcher at HCI Sorbonne julien.gori@cnrs.fr
